properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-25, dev_reflow2 hub session:

"one of the nice things about how I have reflow2 now is the reflow2 design object and the design artifacts live in the same folder/repo. So when I cd to ~/project/reflow2 and then run claude in the terminal, the agent already knows the design object and design artifacts are in the repo together. However, say I have 3 designs (A, B, and C) in the reflow2 mcp at api.flo2.io. ... now say I cd to the folder that has the design artifacts for design A, but I now have 3 designs (A, B, and C) available to the local claude code agent from the remote reflow2 mcp ... how does the agent make the connection that we are discussing design object A and not design object B or C? And maybe as we've been doing with dev_reflow2, the user may want to use the remote hosted design A and B"

THIS IS THE CODE → DESIGN HALF of dec:idea-a-design-apart-from-its-code-knows-where-its-implementation-is, whose mechanism is still unchosen, asked for the case where the design is remote.

⭐ WHAT MAKES IT WORK TODAY IS NOT IMPLICIT, and that is good news: each project's MCP entry says `--graph-path .reflow2/graph` from inside the repo. The folder names its design explicitly; it just names it by PATH. Separation changes the path to an id and a server, and the property can survive intact.

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══

(a) A POINTER FILE IN THE CHECKOUT. A small committed file names the design by id and the server by URL, e.g. design = "<A's id>", server = "https://api.flo2.io". The local client (req:a-local-client-works-against-a-remote-reflow2-server-by-url) reads it when started in that folder, and the session is attached to A and only A. It is today's `--graph-path` with an id in place of a path, which is exactly rule:a-design-is-named-by-an-id-not-a-path. It holds no secret: an id and an address, never a key. CHEAPEST, and closest to how it works now.

(b) THE PER-DESIGN ADDRESS IN THE CLIENT'S OWN CONFIG. api.flo2.io already gives each design its own address (/g/<graph_id>/mcp), so the project's .mcp.json can point at A's address directly. NO reflow2 CODE AT ALL, and it works with the plain sign-in (option a of dec:idea-how-a-local-agent-authenticates-to-api-flo2-io). Against: the link then lives in each agent tool's own config (Claude Code's is not Grok Build's), and reflow2 cannot read it or check it.

(c) ONE CONNECTION, AND THE AGENT WORKS OUT WHICH DESIGN. Connect to the server, see A, B and C, and match the folder to the design whose recorded implementation (its repository) matches this checkout's git remote. Automatic. MEDIUM, and it depends on the design side recording its implementations first.

(d) SEVERAL DESIGNS IN ONE SESSION, for "A and B". The pointer lists more than one, each with its role: A is what this folder implements; B is also open, read-only or writable. The dev_reflow2 hub does this today with one MCP entry per design (child-reflow2, child-flo2, child-cure), so every tool is namespaced by its design and a write cannot land in the other one. This is req:a-session-opens-another-design-without-restarting applied to remote designs; how several are held stays open in dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs.

═══ PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT ═══
· 🛑 WHICH DESIGN A WRITE LANDS IN MUST BE FIXED BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY THE AGENT REMEMBERING. reflow2 already holds this line (ver:a-session-cannot-name-another-design), and so does flo2 (req:a-connector-tool-acts-on-the-design-the-person-names). (c) on its own lets an agent working unattended write into B because it guessed wrong. It is good as a SUGGESTION ("this folder looks like it implements A; attach?") and wrong as the mechanism.
· GUESSING FROM GIT IS FRAGILE: a fork, several remotes, a new repository with no remote yet, one repository implementing two designs, or one design implemented by two repositories (cure may be exactly this). A pointer file and the design's own list of implementations handle all of these; a git-remote match handles the easy case.
· SEVERAL DESIGNS COST CONTEXT. Each design open in a session brings its full tool list; the hub pays this three times over today. (d) should open the second design only when asked.
· THE POINTER IS HALF THE LINK. The design side (option b of the older idea: the design names each implementation once) is the other half, and the client can check the two agree, warning when the folder says A but design A does not list this repository.

A FINDING, NOT A DECISION: (a) plus (d) keeps today's property that the folder says which design it is, works for one design or several, and never guesses. (b) is the zero-code way to try it tomorrow with api.flo2.io. (c) is worth having only as a hint.

═══ SETTLED 2026-09-25 BY ANTHONY: (a) AND (d), WITH (c) AS THE FALLBACK. (b) NOT CHOSEN ═══
Anthony: "keep (a) and (d), with (c) as the fallback."
- (a) A code folder names its design with a small committed pointer file: the design's id and the server's address, never a key.
- (d) The pointer can name several designs with roles: the one this folder implements, and others also open, each namespaced so a write cannot land in the wrong one.
- (c) ONLY WHEN THERE IS NO POINTER, the client offers a match and never picks silently. The rule to reuse is flo2's connector resolver (services/edge-gateway/src/access.ts, dec:a-connector-tool-names-its-design-per-request): search only designs the caller can reach; one clear match is used; several are offered to choose from; none named with several designs means ask. Asked 2026-09-25 how the connector knows "the greenhouse" means backyard-greenhouse-with-aquaponics, this is the answer, and it is the same shape as (c).
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-09-25 — a code folder names its remote design(s) in a committed pointer file, several with roles; with no pointer, the client offers a match and never picks silently
